reason: Under 'Considerations' the two list items state that a Regional custom domain name needs the ACM certificate requested or imported in the same Region as the API, and an edge-optimized one in us-east-1, exactly as claimed.

The What's New post (posted Jun 17, 2025, confirmed by the ACM document history row dated June 17, 2025) says exportable public certificates can be used on EC2 instances, containers or on-premises hosts, and that previously ACM-issued public certificates could only be used with integrated AWS services.

The quote supports kms:Decrypt to read and kms:GenerateDataKey to create or change the value, but it sits in the cross-account walkthrough (key policy for the KMS key in Account1); the quote does not name 'customer managed key' and does not state the rule for the general same-account case the claim implies.

Under 'createSecret: Create a new version of the secret' the page says the method generates a new secret value, stores it with put_secret_value under the staging label AWSPENDING, and that storing it in AWSPENDING helps ensure idempotency.

Under 'finishSecret: Finish the rotation' the page says the function moves AWSCURRENT from the previous version to the new one and Secrets Manager automatically adds AWSPREVIOUS to the previous version to retain the last known good version.
Under the setSecret heading the page says the method changes the credential in the database or service to match the new secret value in the AWSPENDING version, which is the whole claim.
Under 'testSecret: Test the new secret version' the page says the function tests the AWSPENDING version by using it to access the database or service, exactly as claimed.
